perOption.reason: 'Garcia stood outside Frontcountry Mall, waiting for his brother.' Present-participle adjunct whose understood subject is the matrix subject 'Garcia'; Garcia performs the waiting (active relation), so the -ing form is licensed. Grammatical.

perOption.label: (B)
perOption.reason: 'Garcia asked, pointing at a patterned red shirt...' Same participial-adjunct structure; the understood subject 'Garcia' actively points. Grammatical.

perOption.label: (C)
perOption.reason: 'The clerk stopped her work and looked at the clothes, quickly agreeing with Jeff's choice.' Participial adjunct predicated of 'the clerk', who actively agrees. Nothing forces a third finite conjunct ('and agreed'); the adjunct parse is fully well-formed. Grammatical.

perOption.label: (D)
perOption.reason: 'His confidence was, however, quickly was changed to nervousness...' The clause already contains the finite auxiliary 'was' before 'however'; the underlined 'was changed' introduces a second finite 'was', producing *was ... was changed* — two finite verbs in a single clause with no coordination or subordination. No alternative parse rescues it: 'His confidence was' has no complement of its own, 'however' is a connective adverb (not a clause boundary), and no ellipsis/inversion/reduced-relative reading is available. The only repair is the bare past participle 'changed', giving the passive 'was ... quickly changed to nervousness'. Ungrammatical as written.

perOption.label: (E)
perOption.reason: 'everyone fell silent, fascinated by the music.' Past-participle adjunct predicated of 'everyone' with an overt by-phrase agent — everyone is fascinated by the music (passive/psych-participle relation). Grammatical.

note: Clean item from the grammarian lens. The error in (D) is a hard, formally provable double-finite-auxiliary violation (was ... was changed), unambiguous under every reasonable parse. All four distractors are standard participial-adjunct constructions that survive an active search for alternative parses (reduced relatives, absolutes, inversion). Single defensible answer: (D).
